title: Frank Stouffer's Japan offer and the fate of the band
summary: He turned down a contract to Japan in 1935; trumpeter Jimmy Brown died in an internment camp and Jimmy Allen returned in 1938.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Frank Stouffer his name is. And while we were working with them right along there, you know. It wasn't a very hard job. So they got a contract to go to Japan, in 1935.
Oh, I saw you went. I wondered.
So they had some wonderful musicians in that band.
But they did this to make money, you know. So he asked Cal and I would we like to go to Japan, and well, being so young, Japan seemed like to be -- seemed to me like I
was going to heaven or someplace, or going that far away, or going to Mars or something like that.
So right away I said, "No, no, no, Frank, I'm sorry. That's too far."

Which some of them didn't come back, you know, because the war caught them there. And our best trumpet player, Jimmy Brown, he died in a concentration camp. And another, Jimmy Allen, he was a tenor player, he came back in 1938, just before the war started. And I was working at the Savoy Ballroom with Teddy Hill, and I saw Jimmy walk in, and I said, "Hey, Jimmy. My God." He said, "We just got back from Japan." I said, "Oh, wonderful." And there was a Japanese restaurant just next to the Savoy Ballroom, and he walked in and he started speaking Japanese. They hugged him and took him in the kitchen and I didn't see him for about three hours. The Japanese kept him in the kitchen all the time, feeding him and -- because they hadn't heard from home in years.
But Kenny, what -- the other guy stayed?
He settled down there and they put him in a concentration camp after the attack on Pearl Harbor. And
he died in the concentration camp. Oh, they rounded up all the Americans, you know, and put them away like they did the Japanese here -- you know, the Japanese in --
Yeah, they made them labor and everything.
In California, yeah. He just couldn't take it, so -- Jimmy Brown, his name was. He died in -- so Carl and I, doing this --
Carl didn't want to go to Japan.
